data.narrative: The student isolated the check-then-act race condition causing intermittent 500 duplicate key errors using a synthetic 10-concurrency reproduction script. They implemented an atomic PostgreSQL UPSERT with GREATEST() to eliminate both the loud 500 errors and silent timestamp overwrites.

dimension_scores.observation: Formed variable-isolation hypotheses targeting data, timing, and concurrency candidates.
dimension_scores.evidence: Selected concurrency based on high-traffic link error clustering and created targeted reproduction script.

dimension_scores.observation: Extracted unique constraint error signatures from server logs and traced to check-then-act pattern.
dimension_scores.evidence: Identified duplicate key value violates unique constraint analytics_link_id_bucket_unique.

dimension_scores.observation: Authored a minimal 10-concurrency synthetic reproduction script with zero extra moving parts.
dimension_scores.evidence: Created script reproducing 500 errors deterministically on concurrent requests and verified zero errors after fix.

dimension_scores.observation: Maintained clear distinction between loud crash errors and silent data corruption risks.
dimension_scores.evidence: Articulated why silent timestamp overwrites are higher business risk than loud 500 HTTP failures.

dimension_scores.observation: Traced beyond basic retry band-aids to atomic database primitives.
dimension_scores.evidence: Applied PostgreSQL INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET count = count + 1, last_accessed_at = GREATEST(...) to guarantee single-pass atomicity.

dimension_scores.observation: Documented full diagnosis and verification proof as permanent regression testing artifacts.
dimension_scores.evidence: Created progress/module-03-diagnosis.md with exact error signatures, reproduction code, and verification metrics.

strengths: Demonstrated exceptional variable isolation by building a minimal 10-concurrency reproduction script.
Prevented silent data corruption by combining count increment and timestamp updates into a single atomic PostgreSQL UPSERT.

public_evidence.proof: Ran 10-concurrency reproduction script 10 consecutive times -> 0 errors, exact count = 100
